title: Chimor
capsule: Chimor, the Chimú kingdom of Peru's north coast centred on the adobe capital Chan Chan in the Moche Valley, emerged around 900 CE as heir to the earlier Moche (Mochica) cultural tradition in roughly the same coastal territory. During the period covered here the polity was in its formative phase, building the monumental adobe compounds of Chan Chan and developing the irrigation networks, ceramic styles and metalworking traditions that would later underpin its power. According to Chimú oral tradition the kingdom was founded by the culture hero Taycanamo, who arrived by sea on a balsa raft; its dramatic territorial expansion along the coast and its eventual conquest by the Inca lay in later centuries, beyond this window.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Chan Chan's urban layout and Chimor's approximate territorial limits are well established through archaeology; the dynastic sequence and precise dates rely on transcribed oral king lists recorded after Spanish conquest and are subject to substantial revision.
